newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds reverse gains in late selloff.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds reverse gains in late selloff.

text.p: Hedge-fund selling in the U.S. Treasuries market stifled the gentle upward drift that ruled mortgage-backed securities action much of the day, according to traders.
"It looks like there was some hedge-fund selling, and that took us below support," one trader said.
Pass-throughs meandered 1/32 to 5/32 higher overall before turning negative at about 1440 EST/1940 GMT. By 1500 EST/2000 GMT, mortgages had traded off 1/32 to 4/32.
Mortgage-backeds outperformed Treasuries during the selloff, mortgage traders noted.
Dealers purchased some current-coupon paper to be rolled into private-label deals, one trader said. "Current-coupon activity is dominated by CMO-type collection," he said.
In addition, certain higher coupons sold off in the morning "as a result of Fannie Mae prepays," the trader said.
By late on Wednesday, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 5/32 at 99-22/32, yielding 103 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was down 5/32 as well, at 99-18/32 and 99-23/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was off 7/32, yielding 6.59 percent.
